display.purpose: Hero headline only, largest weight in the system.

label.purpose: Rare all-caps micro-labels for genuine category markers, never decorative kickers.

shadows.name: popover
shadows.purpose: The desktop header's mega-menu dropdown only — the system's single shadow use, reserved for genuinely floating panels.

motion.name: reveal-ease
motion.purpose: Staggered scroll-reveal for benefit and audience cards (exponential ease-out, no bounce). Repeats on every viewport entry/exit, not one-shot (20 Aug 2026, requested by name) — the IntersectionObserver stays connected and toggles visibility on every isIntersecting change, so scrolling an element out of view resets it and scrolling back over it replays the reveal. prefers-reduced-motion still forces full visibility regardless of the toggle.

motion.name: scroll-scrub
motion.value: custom property --p (0 to 1), set imperatively from scroll position via requestAnimationFrame
motion.purpose: Drives the Home hero's access-geometry card stack, now its own section directly beneath the headline (not sharing its pinned viewport) with a short 160vh track (~60vh of scroll room): the front card scales down/rotates back/drifts up and left/fades near-zero toward the deck while the card behind it scales up/un-rotates/rises to the front (react-bits' Scroll Stack pattern, two states). Revision 2, 20 Aug 2026 — replaced a plain opacity cross-fade of two bare SVGs plus a separate caption line, which read as text slowly fading in rather than a visible scene change. Revision 3, same day — moved out of the headline's shared viewport (reported as not fitting proportionally) into its own larger section. Revision 4, same day — cards sized larger again, and opacity now runs the full 1-to-0 range (no visible floor) so the inactive card is fully transparent at rest and at scroll-end, not peeking through. Revision 5, same day — the drawn house/bed/lamp/device scene on the 'home' card was replaced with the real Byonyks X-1 product render (same asset as Our Answer, same attribution), composited directly on the card's own background using the PNG's genuine alpha channel (verified by pixel-sampling, not assumed) rather than a white backing plate. Revision 6, same day — the drawn clinic/road/clock scene on the 'in-center' card was replaced with a real hemodialysis machine photo (Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA), on request. Unlike the X-1 render this source wasn't a pre-cut asset, so it was cropped to the gauge/screen panel (removing a cardboard box, tiled wall, and the machine's brand/model label so it reads as generic, not a named-competitor callout), had a faint reflection of a person patched out of the dark monitor, and got a synthetic feathered-alpha edge to match the X-1 render's treatment. Every edit disclosed in public/images/README.md. Bespoke, not a reusable easing token — documented so it isn't reinvented differently elsewhere.

motion.name: reveal-settle
motion.purpose: The single-focal-element counterpart to reveal-ease's rise. Used once, for the X-1 render in Our Answer — not for cards appearing as a list.

motion.name: count-up
motion.purpose: Scroll-triggered numeric count-up, reserved for genuine quantities (the 10,000+ therapies stat only).

narrative.overview: A clinical-trust system that spends almost all of its register in one committed navy and a near-white ground, then uses color the way a hospital uses department signage: not decoration, wayfinding. Every accent beyond navy carries one specific meaning and recurs wherever that meaning applies — gold for "home / India," teal for "clinical evidence," plum for "institutional / formal" — so a visitor who learns the code once (the four benefit cards) reads it instantly the second time (the four audience cards). The system reads as sober and evidence-led first because the Priority-1 and Priority-3 audiences (investors, clinicians) distrust marketing language, and the Priority-2 audience (patients) needs calm, high-contrast legibility over stimulation. Ink navy is not an accent here; on the Home hero it is spent at full page-scale coverage, the system's boldest color move, and everywhere else it recedes to headings and text. Every accent stays rationed to large display type and non-text graphics — never body copy, never small UI. Expanded 20 Aug 2026 from a single-accent system to this four-role one at explicit user request, beyond spec — see deviations.md.
keyCharacteristics: Flat, bordered surfaces over shadowed ones — depth is tonal, not lifted.
Four accent roles (gold, teal, plum, primary blue), each with one fixed meaning, recurring across benefit cards, audience cards, and proof stats.
Every accent is rationed the same way gold always was: large display type and non-text graphics only.
Line-art iconography carries concepts no real image exists for yet; a real, attributed Byonyks asset (the X-1 render) replaces it wherever one exists.
Generous section rhythm keeps a dense, fact-heavy page from feeling cramped.

rules.name: The Full-Bleed Rule
rules.body: Ink navy is used as a whole-section background only in the highest-stakes moments (hero, CTA band) — never as a card fill or small panel.

rules.name: The Accent Ration Rule
rules.body: Each of the four accents (gold, teal, plum, primary-as-accent) appears on large display type, icon chips, or non-text graphics only — never body text, never small UI, never a fifth ad hoc hue.

rules.name: The Wayfinding Rule
rules.body: An accent's meaning is fixed sitewide: gold is always "home/India," teal is always "clinical evidence," plum is always "institutional/formal." Never borrow one for a different meaning because it's visually convenient.

rules.name: The One-Family Rule
rules.body: Every type role is Noto Sans. No second face is introduced for technical or editorial contrast.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Cards and sections separate using a 1px border or a tonal background shift. A shadow is earned only by a genuinely floating element.

dos: Do spend ink navy at full section coverage only for the highest-stakes moments.
Do restrict every accent to large display type, icon chips, and non-text graphics.
Do keep each accent's meaning fixed — reuse an existing role before inventing a fifth hue.
Do separate sections with a border or tonal shift before reaching for a shadow.
Do label illustrative or unsourced content explicitly rather than presenting it as finished.
Do give every interactive element a visible 2px focus ring.
Do prefer a real, correctly-attributed image from Byonyks USA over authored illustration once one exists — caption a render as a render, never as a photograph.
Do give every scroll-driven or auto-playing animation a prefers-reduced-motion path that settles instantly, never a frozen mid-animation frame.
donts: Don't use the destructive red or the logo's kidney-icon red outside error states.
Don't add a kicker or eyebrow label above a heading.
Don't use hard offset shadows, glass/blur effects, gradient text, or bounce/elastic easing.
Don't ship a specific unsourced statistic as a confident claim.
Don't count up a label that isn't a real quantity.
Don't use the semantic pending color as a brand accent, or a brand accent for a pending state.
